proposals.title: Debrief: the guided post-test routine (redo without answers, see why, name the cause, prove it, book check-ins)
proposals.what:
WHERE: the report hero primary for mock, module and diagnostic (and practice sets with 3+ misses): pill "Debrief · 13 misses · about 35 min". Its split menu: "Quick debrief · the 6 worth most points" and the existing "Fix these · 13". Once the debrief is done the primary becomes "Retake as a test · due Sep 30" (or "Fix what's left · 4"). A "Debrief 6 of 13 · Resume" pill sits in the header and on the sittings card, and Today shows "Finish your debrief · 7 left".

FLOW: UI.review in mode 'debrief'. The queue is the misses and blanks, ordered sure-and-wrong first (when confidence tags exist), then by point value (proposal 2), then question order. A step rail reads "Redo · See why · Name it · Prove it".
1. Redo with answers hidden, a stopwatch and no test clock. The student can pick, type or tap "I don't know". It files as repeat=1 (R8: no mastery move) and stores redo_given, redo_right and redo_ms.
2. See why: the original pick against the key, the named misconception of the original pick and of the redo pick ("Different mistake this time" when they differ), every option's reason, and the rationale.
3. Name it: one tap on a cause chip: Fell for the trap (named) · Didn't know how · Slip (knew it, made an error) · Misread the question · Ran out of time · Guessed. One chip is suggested, with an orange outline and the tag "suggested", and Enter accepts it. The rules:
   - a blank after the last answered question of a timed module → Ran out of time
   - conf=guess or attempts.guess → Guessed
   - redo right → Slip ("rushed" when the original took under 0:30)
   - redo wrong with the same reason → Fell for the trap
   - anything else, or "I don't know" → Didn't know how
4. Prove it: an inline twin (same template, fresh seed, source 'twin', cfg.parent = sid), answered normally. Right is a clean answer that counts toward closing the trap. Wrong leads to a worked twin (proposal 7), then a second twin. "Didn't know how" starts with the worked twin.
5. End screen:
   - counts per cause with their point value: "Slips 3 ≈ 30 pts · Traps 7 ≈ 60 · Time 2 ≈ 15 · Didn't know 1 ≈ 10"
   - "Twins right on new numbers: 10 of 13"
   - the traps still open
   - "Check-ins booked" with R9's dates (Sep 26 · 7 questions, Oct 3 · 7, Oct 23 · 7)
   - one next step, chosen by the biggest cause: Slips → habit set (proposal 9); Time → pacing drill (proposal 5); Traps or Didn't know → Fix what's left.

AFTER: Mistakes rows gain a Cause chip plus Redo ✓/✕ and Twin ✓/✕. The review toolbar gains a Cause filter and Colour by Cause. State is saved per question, so the debrief resumes at the next undone miss on any device. The flow is full-screen on a phone.

STUDENT DOES DIFFERENTLY: instead of scanning the grid and closing the tab, they re-solve every miss before seeing the answer, say why it happened, and prove the fix on new numbers in the same sitting.

WHY IT MOVES THE SCORE:
- Retrieval before the reveal (the testing effect) makes the fix stick.
- Separating slips and clock losses from real gaps sends each to the right remedy, instead of re-studying content the student already knows.
- A twin proves transfer, not recognition of a key already seen.
- Spaced check-ins are booked, not hoped for.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's review modal is read-only. Their Hide answers only hides the key and you cannot re-answer. Nothing records why a question was missed, and nothing gives you another question of the same type. Students who follow the tutor's error-log routine keep it in a spreadsheet by hand. Ours makes that routine the default path from the report and records every step.
proposals.needs: F3: UI.review mode 'debrief' (step rail, inline twin tile, worked-twin variant). F4: a table debriefs(learner, session, qid, redo_given, redo_right, redo_ms, cause, cause_suggested, twin_right, at), POST /api/session/{sid}/debrief, and results fields debrief {done, total, by_cause}. R8 repeat for the redo; R9 check-in dates; R24 twin drills. S5: qstate conf, ms and module times for the time rule. S3: Today card. S6: sittings-card status. Point values and next steps come from proposals 2, 5, 7 and 9; each part is left out until its provider lands.

proposals.title: Points on the table: every miss and every skill priced in section points
proposals.what:
PER MISS, on the report: "worth ≈ 12 pts", the midpoint change from re-running scoring.section_score with that one question right on the same route. This generalises the spec's whatif to every question. Module 1 misses near the 60% cut also carry the route: "With this right, Module 1 is 14/22 → the harder Module 2, which lifts the 580 ceiling." The value shows in the cell tooltip and aria-label, on Mistakes rows (a new sort, "Most points"), in the player header, and as a new Colour by "Points" (a 4-step warm-grey ramp). The hero what-if becomes a stacked line, "Easy misses 3 ≈ +40 · Medium 6 ≈ +60 · Hard 4 ≈ +50", each part a filter.

NEW BLOCK "Where your next points are": it replaces the bare Up next on the report and sits above Skills on /results/. One row per skill, sorted by points per minute:
- glyph and skill name
- "≈ +20 pts a section"
- "~25 min to fix"
- evidence: "7 of 12 wrong in 30 days"
- open traps
- [Start 10] (a drill on that topic, open mistakes first)
A footer line against the target: "The top 3 cover 45 of the 60 points to your target."

PRICING, spelled out in a "How this is priced" disclosure. Expected gain = questions of the skill per section × your miss rate on it × points per question at your level.
- Questions per section: a static table from sampling blueprint.module 2,000 times (for example Linear functions 3.1).
- Miss rate: the last 30 answers in the skill, shrunk toward your overall rate with 5 pseudo-answers.
- Points per question: the slope of the scoring anchors at your estimate midpoint, weighted by your usual route's tier mix.
- Minutes = (open owed + 2) × your average time in the skill.
Figures are rounded to 5 and always carry ≈. A skill with fewer than 3 answers shows "Sharpen first" instead of a price.

STUDENT DOES DIFFERENTLY: spends the next hour on the skill that returns the most points per minute, often an Algebra or Advanced Math skill with easy and medium misses, instead of the one that feels worst.

WHY IT MOVES THE SCORE: Math weight is uneven (Algebra and Advanced Math are 70%). Easy and medium misses in frequent skills are the cheapest points, and Module 1 misses near the cut decide the ceiling. Working in order of expected gain reaches the target sooner.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's domain cards show a %, a 7-segment level bar and mislabelled copy ("13% of test section, 1-8 questions"). Their API computes a per-domain domainScore the UI never shows. Their plan asks the student to pick up to 4 Focus areas by feel. Nothing there says what fixing something is worth, or that a Module 1 miss cost the harder route.
proposals.needs: F4: scoring.points_for(questions, answers, qid) and scoring.slope(midpoint, route). F5/S5: a skill_freq table built from blueprint. F4: estimate.py midpoint. S4: the coach and /api/map can take the ranking for Up next. S7: Plan step 4 can pre-suggest focus from it. S3: Today can show the top row.

proposals.title: Sure-but-wrong first: confidence calibration on every report
proposals.what:
BLOCK "#calibration" on the report, after Pace, whenever the sitting has Sure / Unsure / Guess tags (tests with test_confidence on) or I'm guessing flags (practice).

A 3×3 table: rows Sure / Unsure / Guess, columns Right / Wrong / Blank, with counts. Every cell is a review filter. Under it, three callouts:
- "Sure and wrong · 3. You would never have checked these, so they open the debrief."
- "Unsure and right · 5. Fragile points: each gets a check-in in 3 days." (the R9 'unsure' kind, owed 1)
- "Guessed and right · 1. Counted half toward mastery." (R8)
And one line on how far the student can trust "Sure": "When you said Sure you were right 83% (15 of 18). Aim for 95%."

ON /results/:
- Sure accuracy per sitting as dots over the last 10, with a dashed 95% line.
- "Sure and wrong, all time": the misconceptions the student was most often confidently wrong about, each with Fix.

IN THE REVIEW:
- Colour by "Confidence".
- A small S / U / G overlay on each cell.
- A player header tag: "You said: Sure".

TAGS OFF: when the sitting had no tags, the block's place holds one line, "Turn on confidence tags next time to see which answers you were wrongly sure of", with [Turn on], which sets prefs.test_confidence. Suggest to S5 that single-module practice defaults it on, while full sections stay off to match test day.

STUDENT DOES DIFFERENTLY: reviews the answers they were confidently wrong about first, re-checks the lucky ones instead of banking them, and learns when their "sure" deserves a second look on test day.

WHY IT MOVES THE SCORE:
- High-confidence errors are the misconceptions a student never revisits on their own, and correcting them with feedback sticks unusually well (the hypercorrection effect).
- Unsure-but-right points are the ones that disappear on test day.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep collects no confidence at all. Their only self-report is Flagged (n), and it is never evaluated. Our Tests spec already collects the tags (qstate.conf), but the report spec never shows them. This proposal closes that hole.
proposals.needs: S5: qstate.conf and the test_confidence pref (already specified). R8 guess; the R9 unsure trap kind. S6: results summary.calibration {sure, unsure, guess: {right, wrong, blank}} and an /api/stats calibration series. F1: a confidence cell overlay and legend entry. S10: flag calibration shares the block's style.

proposals.title: Retake on new numbers, then a question-by-question 'then vs now'
proposals.what:
BLOCK "#thennow" on every report of a Retake-as-a-test sitting (cfg.like), right after the hero:
- Heading: "Same 44 question types as Section #7 (Sep 23)".
- Four counts, each a filter: Fixed ✕→✓ 9 · Held ✓→✓ 29 · Broke ✓→✕ 2 · Still wrong ✕→✕ 4.
- A paired strip per module: the original cells above, the retake cells below, with the pair's state between them.
- The score line: "520–660 → 600–740 · +80".

FOLLOW-UP:
- "Still wrong" questions are tagged "Persistent" in Mistakes, open the debrief first, and suggest "Didn't know how".
- "Broke" questions open in the player with both attempts side by side (then: pick and time; now: pick and time) and the line "Right on Sep 23. What changed?"

ON THE ORIGINAL REPORT: after its debrief, a chip "Retake due Sep 30" (7 days after the debrief ends, adjustable from 3 to 14). [Remind me] adds a plan task, or a UI.ics event when there is no plan. Once the retake exists, the chip becomes "Retaken Sep 30 · fixed 9 of 13" and links to it.

PAIRING: /api/mock/new {like} stores cfg.pairs {new_qid: src_qid} at draw time.
- Module 1 pairs in order.
- Module 2 pairs by template when the route matches.
- On the other route, only recurring templates pair, and the block says "Module 2 took the other route, so 12 of 22 are paired."

STUDENT DOES DIFFERENTLY: a week after the debrief, they sit the same test content on fresh numbers and get proof of which fixes held under the clock.

WHY IT MOVES THE SCORE:
- A parallel form measures learning, not memory of answers.
- A delayed retake is spaced retrieval.
- "Fixed 9" rewards the review work, and "Still wrong 4" isolates the persistent gaps worth more time.
proposals.beats: A TopTierPrep retake re-serves the same fixed paper (Pro includes 10 retakes a month), so a higher score may just be remembered answers. A retake is only marked "Practice test — not ranked", with no link to the first attempt and no per-question comparison.
proposals.needs: S5: mock/new like (already specified) plus cfg.pairs. S6: a results field thennow {pairs, counts, delta}. S7: a plan task for the retake (else F1's UI.ics). F3: a side-by-side attempt view in the player (reusing UI.history rows).

proposals.title: Your bail-out time: pacing rules from your own clock
proposals.what:
ON /results/, a "#pacing" block (and a compact line on each timed report): accuracy by time spent, from every timed first-try answer in tests and timed drills.
- Buckets 0–0:30 · 0:30–1:35 · 1:35–2:40 · 2:40–4:00 · 4:00+, split by tier, drawn as bars with n.
- Bail-out time = the start of the first bucket at 1:35 or later where the student's accuracy is under 35%, with n ≥ 8. A blind guess on 4 options is 25%, and the minutes saved buy another question.
- Headline: "Past 2:40 you're right 22% of the time (9 of 41). At 2:40, mark it, guess, move on."
- Before 40 timed answers: "Needs 40 timed answers · 17 so far."

ON EACH TIMED REPORT, in Pace:
- A pacing what-if in points: "Time sinks: 4 questions past your 2:40 took 13:20, and 1 was right. The 2 blanks at the end of Module 2 were Easy and Medium, where you're right 85% in about 1:05. With that time: about +2 questions ≈ +20 pts." Each clause is a filter.
- "Wrong answers took 1:58 on average, right ones 1:12", next to the spec's rushed-misses chip.

ACTIONS:
- [Pacing drill · 12 questions]: a timed drill at the 95 s pace (R34), drawn from the templates where the student solves slowly. At the bail-out time a quiet in-question cue appears ("2:40 · mark, guess, move on", no alarm). The summary shows each bail decision and its outcome.
- [Use my bail-out in tests] sets a pref, so the test runner's pace guide shows the same cue.

STUDENT DOES DIFFERENTLY: follows a personal cutoff derived from their own data instead of sinking 5 minutes into one hard question, and practises the bail-out under a clock.

WHY IT MOVES THE SCORE: time spent on low-probability questions comes out of reachable ones. Blanks and rushed end-of-module answers are points lost to clock management, not to content, and they are the fastest points to recover.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's report has no time per question at all. Their contest Time Analysis ("average seconds per answered question, by difficulty") only averages, and it was empty. Nothing links time to accuracy or gives a rule.
proposals.needs: R7: attempts.ms for tests. F4: progress.pacing(learner) returning buckets and bail. S6: results pacing_whatif. F5: drill body field `bail` (seconds) and source 'pacing'. F3: the runner cue. S5: the test pace guide reads the new pref.

proposals.title: Sharpen: evidence meters and 6-question probes that turn a hint into a verdict
proposals.what:
EVIDENCE METER on every domain card and skill row (report, and the Skill panel on /results/):
- 3 pips: Low (under 6 answers in 60 days) · Some (6–15) · Solid (16+).
- Accuracy with an 80% Wilson interval: "43% · likely 25–62%".

SHARPEN: low-evidence rows get [Sharpen · 6 questions · ~9 min]. It runs as an inline probe in the review player:
- source 'probe', cfg.parent = sid
- adaptive: true, pool untried
- tiers bracketing the student's level
- no clock, instant feedback
Afterwards the card updates in place, for example:
- "Linear inequalities: 1/2 on the test + 5/6 sharpening → Getting there · Some evidence. The test miss looks like a slip."
- "2/6 → a real gap. It's now first in Where your next points are."

KNOCK-ON CHANGES:
- The points list (proposal 2) prices no low-evidence skill and shows "Sharpen first" instead.
- The coach never makes a skill a focus off one sitting's 1–2 questions.
- The report's domain helper becomes specific: "Algebra: 15 questions · Solid. Geometry: 7 · Some."

STUDENT DOES DIFFERENTLY: spends 9 minutes confirming a suspected weakness before spending hours on it, and stops drilling a skill that one bad question made look weak.

WHY IT MOVES THE SCORE: a 44-question section carries 1–4 questions per skill, so single-sitting skill results are mostly noise. Unlimited fresh items make targeted measurement cheap, so study time goes to real gaps.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep grades domains off 1–8 questions with no uncertainty. Their review payload has no skill at all, so they cannot even say which skill a miss belonged to, and a finite bank cannot afford probe questions.
proposals.needs: F5: drill with adaptive, pool untried and topics, plus source 'probe' added to R24's inline list and counted on the parent. F4: progress.evidence(learner, topic) with the interval. S6: evidence on results domains/topics and on /api/skill. S4: the coach respects evidence.

proposals.title: Study one, solve one: worked twins for misses you didn't know how to do
proposals.what:
IN THE PLAYER: next to "Try one like this", a secondary "Study one first". The debrief uses it automatically when the cause is "Didn't know how" or the redo was wrong.

STUDY ONE: a fresh seed of the same template, shown worked:
- the stem and figure, with the key marked
- the rationale expanded with this seed's numbers
- every wrong option with its misconception ("B comes from adding the base and the height")

NOW YOU: another fresh seed to answer, through the twin drill.
- Wrong again → a second study-and-solve pair.
- Wrong after that → "Step down": one easier template in the same skill.

NO LEAKS: worked seeds come from GET /api/types/{t}/example (seed range 900000+, never served in practice), so studying one never uses up a real question or reveals a key the student will meet later.

TRACKING: the player shows "Studied 1 · solved 1 · right", and the Mistakes row shows "Worked example used".

LATER: once templates carry step lists (a bank change), add faded examples. The second pair hides the last step, then the last two, before a full solve.

STUDENT DOES DIFFERENTLY: studies a solved, matched problem right before solving one, instead of reading one explanation of the question they got wrong and moving on.

WHY IT MOVES THE SCORE: for a learner who lacks the method, studying a worked example and then solving a matched problem teaches more than solving alone (the worked-example effect). A matched pair on new numbers is something only an unlimited bank can hand out.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep gives one long "Justification" for the missed item and nothing to practise the same type with. A fixed bank cannot produce a matched second problem without spending one of its own items.
proposals.needs: F5: GET /api/types/{t}/example (already specified). F3: a worked variant of the inline twin tile. R24: twin drills. T-bank: a rationale-steps field, later, for faded steps.

proposals.title: Between tests: what your practice has earned, and whether you're on track
proposals.what:
ON /results/, a top row beside the estimate, "Since Section #7 (6 days)":
- mistakes closed: 11 (≈ +55 pts, priced as in proposal 2)
- check-ins held: 4 of 5
- skills up a mastery word: 2 (Linear functions: Learning → Getting there)
- 142 questions · 3 h 10 m
- a clearly labelled practice-based line: "From practice since: about 560–700 (not a test)".

ON EACH NEW SCORED REPORT, under the delta chip, the result against what practice predicted:
- Inside the band: "Expected from your practice: 540–680 · got 520–660 · inside the usual swing of ±70."
- Outside it: "70 below what your practice predicts. Check Pace and the debrief for slips."
A noisy drop is named as noise, not as failure.

TRAJECTORY (with 3+ scored sittings over 7+ days):
- The score chart draws a projection cone from a weighted fit of midpoints to the exam date.
- One line: "At +12 a week you reach about 590–710 by Oct 3. Target 700 needs +18 a week. The top 3 in Where your next points are cover 45 of the 60."
- With fewer sittings: "Two more scored sittings give you a projection."

AT THE END OF THE REPORT: "This sitting's debrief closed 7 mistakes ≈ +35 pts", plus the streak from progress.days.

STUDENT DOES DIFFERENTLY: keeps going after a flat or lower test, because the report shows the work already banked and says when a drop is within normal variation. They also see the weekly gain the target needs.

WHY IT MOVES THE SCORE: consistent daily practice is the biggest driver, and students quit when a noisy test hides real progress. A projection with the required rate turns a target into a weekly amount of work.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's Score Overview stays empty until a full four-module test. The profile Score Trend reads "Latest: 0". Their plan wizard's "about 200 points per week" is arithmetic on the target, not a measured rate. Nothing shows progress between tests, and nothing explains a drop.
proposals.needs: F4: estimate.practice_estimate (topic mastery × skill frequency through the scoring anchors, ±100) and a trend fit in estimate.py. R9: a timeline of closed traps and held check-ins. R13: progress.days. S6: /api/stats fields since_last and projection. Pricing from proposal 2. R15: target and exam date.

proposals.title: Habit families: the error you make in every topic
proposals.what:
THE MAP: the ~1,300 misconception labels, reviewed by hand, sorted into about 12 cross-topic habits:
- Answered a different quantity than asked
- Sign or direction flipped
- Inverted a ratio, fraction or slope
- Decimal or percent place
- Read the wrong part of a graph, table or chart
- Left out a step or term (the ½, the constant, the starting amount)
- Mixed up two formulas (sin/tan, area/perimeter)
- Treated a sample as the population
- Counted solutions wrong
- Arithmetic slip
Labels that fit no habit stay without one.

ON THE REPORT, a "#habits" block after Mistakes, one row per habit present, for example:
- "Answered a different quantity than asked · 4 here (M1 Q6, M2 Q3, M2 Q9, M2 Q15) · 11 all time across 5 skills"
- a one-line rule written per habit: "Before choosing, reread the last line and circle what it asks for."
- [Habit set · 10]: a drill across that habit's templates, with `want` set to its reasons, so every question contains the trap.

ON /results/, "Your habits": the top 3 habits by hits in 30 days, each with a weekly-hits sparkline. A falling line means the habit is fading.

ELSEWHERE: the debrief's Slip cause links to the matching habit, and the Review pane (S10) names it.

STUDENT DOES DIFFERENTLY: fixes one checking habit that pays off in every topic, instead of repairing the same kind of error template by template.

WHY IT MOVES THE SCORE: many "careless" losses are one repeated behaviour. Naming it with evidence across skills, and drilling items that all contain the trap, builds the habit where generic "be careful" advice fails.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's Distractor Analysis is free prose per item with no names that repeat, so it can never see a pattern across questions, and their report has no skill data at all. Review's norm matching (79 misconceptions recurring across templates) finds exact repeats; habit families go a level up.
proposals.needs: T-bank: Mis.tag, or server/habits.json mapping label/norm to habit (keyword rules, then hand review). F4: progress.norm (R9). F5: a `want`-regex drill across templates. S6: results and /api/stats field habits. S10: a habit line in the Review pane.

proposals.title: Put this report into my week
proposals.what:
BLOCK "#week" at the end of the report, replacing the lone Up next: a 7-day proposal built from this sitting. Every row can be edited or removed. Then [Add to my plan] (with an active plan) or [Add to Today] (without one, shown in Today's list), plus "Add reminders to my calendar" (UI.ics).

DEFAULT ROWS:
- Day 0–1: finish the debrief, if it isn't done.
- Days 1–5: the top 3 rows of Where your next points are, as 10–15-question sets, interleaved (order mixed, at most 2 skills per domain, as the coach deals them).
- Day 2: a habit set, if a habit had 3 or more hits.
- Days 3 and 10: this sitting's check-ins (pool checks).
- Day 7: Retake as a test (like: sid), 70 min, or one module (35 min) when the daily minutes are under 70.

FIT: rows fit the plan's daily minutes and rest days (R15), and the block states the load: "About 25 min a day."

STUDENT DOES DIFFERENTLY: leaves the report with a scheduled, spaced, interleaved week instead of an intention.

WHY IT MOVES THE SCORE: spaced, interleaved repair beats repairing everything in one massed session, and a concrete schedule is what actually gets done.
proposals.beats: TopTierPrep's plan reacts to tests only through a "score drift" banner (60+ points up) and a Rebalance button, and their generator failed 3 times out of 3 in the live walk. Their report offers no next action at all.
proposals.needs: S7: plan task create/patch (plan_tasks, R14) with task tags YYYY-MM-DD:(fix|recheck|focus|test). F5: drill source 'plan'. S3: Today's list. R9: due dates. Rows come from proposals 1, 2, 4 and 9; each row is left out until its provider exists.

parity_gaps.spec_says: "62% of students here scored at or below you on their first section (148 students)". A pill "Ranked · your first section" or "Not ranked · retake #3". Hidden below 20 first sittings.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: It is the same statistic as their "N% scored at or below you on their first attempt", with the same ranked / not-ranked rule. Ours only adds the n. It ranks one moment and says nothing about progress.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Add a growth percentile: among students here whose first section was within ±30 of the student's, the median change after the same number of days, and where the student stands ("Started 520–660 like 41 students: their median after 4 weeks is +40; you're at +90, ahead of 80%"), shown once n ≥ 20. Also add the College Board's published national Math percentile for the midpoint, labelled with its source and year (open question 3.5.9).

parity_gaps.spec_says: Math gauge only. The caption reads "Reading and Writing is not on SAT Freshman yet"; left as an open question.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: This is below theirs (Total 420/1600): a student cannot see their total against a college target.
parity_gaps.upgrade: When an R&W number exists, show an estimated total. The R&W value comes from rw_now (Plan/Me, R15) or the latest R&W in outside_scores (S3's Add a score). It shows as a second gauge segment, "R&W 620 · self-reported Sep 12 · Update", with "Total about 1140–1280". Without one, show "Add your R&W score to see a total".

parity_gaps.spec_says: %, "11 of 15 correct", a difficulty-weighted 7-segment level, the share of the section, a delta, and "Missed most" topics.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: It is their card (%, 7-segment bar, share), correctly labelled. It describes the domain but never says what it costs or how reliable the reading is.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Add "≈ 45 pts lost here" (the sum of per-question point values, proposal 2), an evidence meter with Sharpen (proposal 6), and "Next: Linear inequalities ≈ +20" linking to the points list.

parity_gaps.spec_says: Hide answers persists across Previous/Next with an "Answers hidden" chip. A pick while hidden reveals locally "without filing anything".
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: It matches their Hide answers (persists, shows a chip). The re-pick is thrown away, so the report never learns whether the student can now solve it. §1.13's "without filing anything" also contradicts R21 ("re-answer files a repeat"), and R21 wins.
parity_gaps.upgrade: File the hidden re-pick as a repeat (R8) and summarise the results: "Right on a calm redo: 5 of 11. Those were slips, not gaps", in the hero and on Mistakes rows. Open "Review mistakes" with answers hidden by default, so the student retrieves before seeing (one key shows them). The Debrief (proposal 1) is the guided form of this.

parity_gaps.spec_says: A --tile card headed "Explanation" with the rationale in serif, plus every wrong option's misconception.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: Our per-option labels beat their Distractor Analysis, but the correct path is one sentence (for example "A = ½bh with b = 39, h = 58 gives 1,131"). That is thinner than their long-form Justification, so a student who didn't know the method gets less than on TopTierPrep.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Add "Show the working": numbered steps rendered per template from item.params (the audit solver already re-derives the key from those numbers). Add a "Faster way" line per template family where one exists (Desmos, plugging in the choices, backsolving) with "saves about 0:40". Add "Study one first" worked twins (proposal 7).

parity_gaps.spec_says: Question ID template · seed with Copy; domain, skill, difficulty word, format, time and position.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: These are the same fields as their Details popover (ID, domain, skill, difficulty) plus time. Difficulty is still only the Easy/Medium/Hard label, while they have a 1–7 Question Score.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Show the measured level (QBank's levels 1–7, from 20+ first tries), "Students here: 78% right first try · median 1:05", and "You on this type: 3 of 5". Use the same data in the report to mark "a miss most students get right" (a cheap point) apart from "31% get this right".

parity_gaps.spec_says: Built to be "at least as capable as theirs": a Sent-with-your-report box, a prefilled title with counter, categories, details, screenshots, a Reported chip, and the toast "we check every one".
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: It is designed to parity, and as on theirs a key dispute waits for a human.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Check instantly on submit for "Wrong answer key", "Two answers are right" and grid-in disputes. The server regenerates the (template, seed), runs the topic's independent audit solver, and returns the result with the working ("Our independent checker re-derived D from 73 and 111: …"). For a grid-in, grid_equal and accepted_forms say whether the entry was equivalent and why it was refused. If the checker disagrees, the report is flagged urgent and the attempt marked disputed (R8, out of mastery). The sitting is re-marked once the item is fixed, and the reply lands in Settings.

parity_gaps.spec_says: "Math 540–680", a confidence pill with its reason, a trend chip, and latest / best / target / exam date.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: It has the same parts as their Estimated Score card (range, confidence level with reason, trend), plus context.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Add a "What would raise it" action ("One full section this week makes it High · 70 min · Start"). Add the practice-based line between tests and the projection to exam day (proposal 8).

parity_gaps.spec_says: Easy/Medium/Hard rows with "avg 0:58", and on the overview "Average time: easy 0:58 · medium 1:31 · hard 2:24 (test pace 1:35)".
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: It is their contest Time Analysis ("average seconds per answered question, by difficulty") moved onto the report. Averages without accuracy don't tell the student what to do.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Add accuracy by time spent, the personal bail-out time, time on right vs wrong answers, and the pacing what-if in points (proposal 5).

parity_gaps.spec_says: The grid's Colour by: Status | Difficulty | Time, each with a legend.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: It extends their QBank overview's Status | Difficulty toggle by one view.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Add Points (which misses cost the most), Confidence (proposal 3) and Cause (after the debrief), each with its legend and counts.

parity_gaps.spec_says: The tile "Flagged 3 · 2 of them wrong", a Flagged filter, and a flag overlay on cells.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: It is their Flagged (n) filter and legend count, plus a wrong count.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Say whether flagging paid off, from the qstate trail: "Flagged 3: returned to 2, changed 1 wrong → right; the one you didn't return to was wrong." Add S10's calibration line on the report: "Your flags are wrong 67% of the time. Return to them before the end."

parity_gaps.why_only_parity: It is the same count theirs shows (though ours, correctly, never calls a blank Incorrect).
parity_gaps.upgrade: Say what the blanks cost and why: "2 blanks. A guess on each was worth ≈ 3 pts; both came at the end of Module 2 with 0:00 left". Link to Pace, with a what-if for guessing on every blank.

parity_gaps.spec_says: Relative time, kind and seq, score and delta, duration, wrong/blank chips per module, open count, twins, and Review / Fix.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: It is their review card (paper, time, wrong-number chips, Review) with the score added back.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Show the post-test work on each card: "Debrief 6 of 13 · Resume" or "Debriefed · 10 of 13 twins right", and "Retake due Sep 30" or "Retaken: fixed 9 · broke 2". The list then doubles as a to-do list.

parity_gaps.spec_says: Bands with a trend line, a target line, an estimate zone, tooltips and range/kind filters; a separate 14-day activity chart.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: It is a better-drawn version of their Score Trend plus the study-time calendar, still shown as two unrelated facts.
parity_gaps.upgrade: Overlay weekly practice minutes and mistakes closed under the score chart on the same x-axis. Add the projection cone to exam day (proposal 8), so effort and result read together.
